title: Cratylus's branching, commit and push conventions
situation: The operator restated cratylus's working conventions: Git flow's dev/main split in place of GitHub flow with a pull request per task into dev.
decision: Cratylus follows Git flow's dev/main split, without release or hotfix branches. Each change is made on a short-lived branch from dev and merged locally into dev once the one check passes on the merged result. Release is a pull request from dev into main, and it is the operator's. Nothing is committed to main directly. Commit autonomously at natural boundaries between gates, never past one; pushing a branch needs no say-so. Commit only your own paths, by name; never amend or rewrite shared history.
consequences: The repository's working conventions already state this; the history concept follows.
